item.title: Tesla warranty explained: what is covered in the US, UK and Europe, from the battery to used cars
item.description: Four years for the car, eight for the battery, and different mileage limits on each side of the Atlantic. A plain guide to Tesla's warranties, the 70% battery promise, used-car cover and your legal rights in Europe.

item.title: Who sits on Tesla's board in 2026? The nine directors, their ties to Musk and how independent they are
item.description: Tesla's board decides on Elon Musk's pay and the SpaceX merger question. Here is who the nine directors are, which links Tesla considers harmless, and why critics still question the board's independence.

item.title: Tesla maintenance schedule: what servicing your Tesla really needs, and how often
item.description: No oil changes and no mandatory annual service, but tyres, filters, brake fluid and brakes still need attention. Tesla's recommended intervals for Model 3, Model Y, Model S and Model X, in plain language.

item.title: How much does a Tesla Supercharger cost in 2026? US prices by state, and 6 ways to pay less
item.description: Supercharger prices in the US have crept up this year, with big differences between states and between members and non-members. Here is what a charge costs now, and how to keep the bill down.

item.title: Tesla Optimus history: the humanoid robot's road from 2021 reveal to 2026 production
item.description: Five years ago Optimus was an idea on a stage. Now Tesla says it is building production-quality robots in Fremont. A clear timeline of every key step, promise and delay.

item.title: Starlink vs Amazon Leo: where the satellite internet race stands in October 2026
item.description: Starlink has about 11,100 satellites and 13.6 million subscribers. Amazon's Leo has fewer than 400 satellites and has not launched service yet. Here is how the two compare, and why it matters for Tesla.

item.title: Tesla's Megafactories explained: Lathrop, Shanghai and Texas, and their 110 GWh of Megapack capacity
item.description: Tesla now builds its Megapack grid batteries in three dedicated plants on two continents. Here is what each one does, how big they are and why the network matters.

item.title: Tesla Sentry Mode explained: how it works, how much battery it uses, and the privacy rules in Europe
item.description: Sentry Mode turns a parked Tesla into a security camera. Here is how it works, what USB drive you need, how much range it costs per day, and why the rules are stricter in Europe.

item.title: Tesla's deals with Musk's other companies: every related-party transaction in the 2026 proxy
item.description: Megapacks for xAI, Cybertrucks for SpaceX, ads on X and a $2 billion SpaceX stake: Tesla's proxy statement lists what it bought from and sold to companies linked to Elon Musk and its directors.

item.title: How to check your Tesla's battery health: the built-in test, what the result means and how to slow degradation
item.description: Teslas can now measure their own battery health. A step-by-step guide to running the test, reading the percentage, and the charging habits Tesla recommends to keep your battery healthy.

item.title: Powerwall 3 vs Powerwall 3P: which Tesla home battery fits your home?
item.description: Tesla now sells two versions of its home battery: the single-phase Powerwall 3 and the three-phase Powerwall 3P for Europe. Here is how they differ in power, solar inputs and backup, and which one suits which home.

item.title: NACS explained: how Tesla's plug became SAE J3400, and which EVs can use Superchargers now
item.description: Tesla's charging plug is now the North American standard, known officially as SAE J3400. Here is how that happened, what the plug can do, which brands can Supercharge, and why none of this applies in Europe.

item.title: Nashville's Music City Loop reaches downtown, but a new report warns of sinkholes, flooding and pollution in the rock ahead
item.description: The Boring Company's tunnel under Nashville has reached the Music City Center. A hydrogeology report says the hardest limestone, with caves and contaminated sites nearby, is still to come.

item.title: How to ride a Tesla Robotaxi: the app, the seven cities, prices and what to expect
item.description: Planning to try a driverless Tesla? Here is a practical guide to the Robotaxi app, where the service runs, what a ride costs, how the Cybercab differs from a Model Y, and the limits to know before you go.

item.title: How Tesla trains Optimus: camera helmets, human videos and 500,000 hours of data
item.description: Tesla teaches its humanoid robot mostly by filming people at work, not by steering it remotely. Here is how the method works, how it changed, and where it still falls short.

item.title: How Starlink works: satellites, laser links, dishes and ground stations explained
item.description: A plain-language guide to how SpaceX's Starlink gets internet from space to your home, phone or car, why it is faster than older satellite services, and what that means for Tesla.

item.title: Grok in your Tesla and your privacy: who processes your conversations, and which cars qualify
item.description: Grok conversations in a Tesla are handled by SpaceX's AI division, not by Tesla. Here is what Tesla says about anonymity, location and contacts, and which cars and connections you need.

item.title: Giga New York explained: what Tesla actually does at its Buffalo factory
item.description: Tesla's Buffalo plant was meant to be a giant solar factory. Today it makes Supercharger parts and energy products, assembles a new solar panel and labels data for FSD. Here is how it got there.

item.title: Why the Cybertruck and Starship are both made of stainless steel: the shared metal behind Tesla and SpaceX
item.description: Tesla's pickup and SpaceX's rocket share more than an owner. Both use cold-worked stainless steel developed by a materials team that worked for both companies. Here is how that came about.

item.title: Tesla vs GM in Q3 2026: GM earned four times more, yet Tesla is worth over 20 times as much
item.description: General Motors and Tesla reported third-quarter results a day apart. Side by side, the numbers show two very different companies, and why investors value them so differently.

item.title: Tesla's quiet growth engine: 'services and other' revenue jumps 33% and profit doubles in Q3 2026
item.description: Used cars, repairs, Supercharging and insurance now bring in $4.6 billion a quarter for Tesla. Gross profit from the segment doubled to a record $734 million. Here is what is in it and why it matters.

item.title: Project Crystal Sun: Tesla's $10.1 billion solar cell factory plan, and where it stands now
item.description: Tesla is weighing a giant solar factory near Houston that would make everything from silicon ingots to finished panels. A local school board approved a tax deal in September, and Tesla's latest filing confirms solar manufacturing is on its agenda. Here is what is known.

item.title: Can you buy a Tesla Optimus? Price, release date and who gets the robot first
item.description: Tesla has started building Optimus, but there is still no price and no way to order one. Here is the latest timeline from Tesla's Q3 2026 call: factories first, business customers around the end of 2027, homes later.

item.title: Tesla's factories can build 2.5 million cars a year. In Q3 they ran at a pace of about 1.86 million
item.description: Tesla's latest capacity table shows room for more than 2.5 million vehicles a year, after Giga Texas got a bigger Model Y rating. Actual output is well below that, and most of the spare room sits outside China. Here is the plant-by-plant picture.

item.title: Tesla Halloween Mode explained: Trick or Treat, the ghost car and the Fright Show, and why some Teslas miss out
item.description: Tesla's software update 2026.38.3 added a Halloween Mode with spooky sounds, a ghost costume and a light show. Here is how to turn it on, what it does, the Sentry Mode catch, and which cars do not get it.

item.title: Starlink in India: licensed but still waiting for spectrum, while Tesla's Model Y slowly gains ground
item.description: India has approved the spectrum pricing for satellite internet, but Starlink still cannot launch. How the two Musk companies are faring in India, and why their stories are linked.

item.title: SpaceX wants a million AI satellites in orbit: why most Terafab chips, and Tesla's AI7, are meant for space
item.description: SpaceX has filed for up to one million computing satellites and shown its first design, AI1. Here is the plan, the obstacles, and how Terafab and Tesla's chip roadmap tie into it.

item.title: Tesla tyres explained: T markings, noise foam, rotation and winter rules in Europe
item.description: Electric cars are hard on tyres. What the T0 marking on a Tesla tyre means, how often to rotate, why EVs wear tyres faster, and the winter tyre rules if you drive to the Alps.

item.title: Musk's 2018 Tesla pay package: how the eight-year court fight ended, and what it changed
item.description: A shareholder with nine Tesla shares sued in 2018. Eight years later Musk has exercised the options, Tesla got $1 in damages and the company has moved to Texas. The full timeline.

item.title: Macrohard explained: the Tesla and SpaceXAI 'Digital Optimus' project, seven months on
item.description: Musk's 'Digital Optimus' is meant to do office work on Tesla's AI4 chip with Grok as the brain. What the joint project is, why it matters for Tesla, and why there is still no product.
